question: Should OpenClaw adopt deny-over-allow rules on both `tools.exec.denylist` and host-local `exec-approvals.json`, with matches forcing human-only one-shot approval even under `security=full` and `ask=off`?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but it creates persisted configuration and protocol surface while changing the privileged exec authorization contract; automation cannot accept that permanent boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt the dual-layer contract
options.body: Keep both policy surfaces, require security-owner approval, resolve conflicts, and merge only after integrated exact-head companion proof.

options.title: Use host approvals only
options.body: Remove `tools.exec.denylist` and keep the STOP list solely in host-local approvals state to minimize policy ownership.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Defer or close the PR if maintainers do not want deny-over-allow to override permissive execution policy.

recommendation.title: Adopt the dual-layer contract
recommendation.body: Keep both policy surfaces, require security-owner approval, resolve conflicts, and merge only after integrated exact-head companion proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is the best evidence-backed owner for a cross-host exec-policy and security-contract decision.
